title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-18
content:
Context / summary:
- User-reported regression in hosted API throughput and increased p99 latency after deploy on 2024-11-14 03:10 UTC (deploy id: canary-20241114-03).
- Symptoms: sustained throughput drop (~55% of baseline) under steady client load; median batch sizes observed by batcher decreased from ~12 to ~3; p99 latency increased from ~45ms -> ~210ms.
- Impact: degraded real-time chat and streaming endpoints for multiple customers (ticketed under INFR-893).

Quick timeline:
- 2024-11-14 02:55 UTC: Canary deploy started.
- 2024-11-14 03:10 UTC: Canary promoted to 20% traffic. First customer reports.
- 2024-11-14 03:20 UTC: Alerts: high p99 latency/service-level SLO breaches.
- 2024-11-14 03:45 UTC: Rollback to previous release on all serving nodes for affected region. Partial recovery seen but not full; follow-up investigation shows config change persisted in cluster config store.

What changed in release (observable):
- PR 472 changed batching window and added per-route max_batch_timeout_ms override and a config migration that defaults to 0 (meaning "prefer immediate flush" unless set). The migration logic may have set per-route timeout to 0 for some routes.
- New kernel selection heuristic (opt-kernel-2) enabled on a subset of instances (non-RTX fleet) — might be orthogonal but callout here.

Observed metrics (from console + node-debug logs):
- Baseline throughput (before deploy): 1200-1500 requests/sec (aggregate), median batch size: 11.8, 95th batch size: 24.
- During incident: throughput 600-700 req/sec, median batch size: 3.1, 95th batch size: 6.
- CPU on batcher processes low (20-35%), GPU utilization roughly unchanged; latency per-token CPU-bound tasks increased.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from 72% -> 21% for affected model route (route: text-chat-v1).

Logs / error snippets (redacted):
- batcher.log:
  [2024-11-14T03:12:07Z] WARN  batcher: flush_interval=0ms; batch building ended early; queued=2; built_batch_size=2
  [2024-11-14T03:12:09Z] INFO  rpc: dispatching request id=... route=text-chat-v1 latency_ms=220
  [2024-11-14T03:12:10Z] DEBUG kernel-selector: selected=opt-kernel-2 for model=redwood/t5x-small

- node-debug snippets (observed on node id=rnode-14):
  KVCacheStats: hits=42 misses=158 total=200 hit_rate=0.21
  BatcherQueue: add_time=10.2ms wait_time_median=12.4ms flush_policy=immediate

Commands / reproductions I ran locally:
1) Simple curl-based load (to simulate single-route steady RPS):
   for i in $(seq 1 400); do curl -s -X POST "https://canary.local/api/v1/complete" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\",\"max_tokens\":16}'; done &
   - Measured median batch size by reading /metrics endpoint (batcher.batch_size.histogram) -> matches low batch size when per-route timeout is 0.

2) wrk micro-bench (100 connections, 50 threads, fixed RPS) against a test route:
   wrk -t50 -c100 -d60s -R800 http://rnode-14.internal/route/text-chat-v1
   - Observed lower aggregate req/sec and p99 jump; confirmed reduced batching.

3) Local unit-run reproducer (python):
   # minimal reproducer: 
   from client import RedwoodClient
   c = RedwoodClient(base_url='http://localhost:8080')
   for _ in range(500):
       resp = c.complete(route='text-chat-v1', prompt='test', max_tokens=16)

   - Instrumented batcher metrics via DEBUG endpoint showed flush_interval == 0 for this route.

Hypotheses:
- H1: The config migration that sets per-route max_batch_timeout_ms defaulted to 0 for many routes (effectively disabling batching). With immediate flush policy, requests are flushed as soon as they arrive -> small batch sizes -> lower GPU throughput and higher p99.
- H2: opt-kernel-2 selection has a different latency profile and interacts poorly with small batches (high per-request overhead) — amplifies regression when batching disabled.
- H3: KV cache misconfiguration (eviction policy or namespace mismatch) reduced cache hits, increasing work per request and reducing opportunity for batching benefits. The drop in cache hit-rate supports this but likely secondary.

Quick checks to validate H1/H2/H3:
- Check config store (etcd/consul) for per-route settings: looked at /config/routes/text-chat-v1 -> max_batch_timeout_ms: 0 (unexpected).
- Rollback attempt: set max_batch_timeout_ms to 50ms for a canary subset; observed median batch size climb back to ~10 and throughput recover to ~95% baseline on canary.
- Kernel revert: forced kernel-selector to prefer opt-kernel-1 for a node; small improvement but not full recovery unless batch timeout > 0. Suggests H1 primary.

Repro steps for eng on-call / SRE to replicate in staging quickly:
1) Deploy the config migration that sets max_batch_timeout_ms to 0 (or patch consul entry) for route text-chat-v1.
2) Run wrk at R ~ 800 against route on staging serving nodes.
3) Collect metrics: batcher.batch_size.{p50,p95}, batcher.flush_interval, kvcache.hit_rate, gpu_util, p99_latency.
4) Flip per-route timeout to 50ms and observe metrics return.

Root cause (working theory):
- The migration in PR 472 defaulted per-route max_batch_timeout_ms to 0 for routes that did not explicitly set a timeout. The runtime interprets 0 as "flush immediately" which defeats continuous batching. This reduces average batch size and dramatically increases per-request overhead on CPU with small batches, causing throughput regression. opt-kernel-2 made the symptoms worse but not root cause.

Temporary mitigations implemented:
- Manual override: updated consul key for affected routes to max_batch_timeout_ms=50 (rolling rewrite) at 2024-11-14 04:10 UTC. Canary tests show recovery.
- Rollback of PR 472 migration flagged (need safe migration path).

Permanent remediation suggestions:
- Change migration logic: default should be null/absent -> fallback to global default (e.g., 50ms) not explicit 0. Add explicit sentinel value for "disabled" instead of using 0.
- Add configuration validation in deploy pipeline to reject zero-value timeouts unless explicitly opted-in (two-step: PR must set route-level flag).
- Add SLO/metric alert for median batch size drop per-route (if p50 batch size drops >50% relative to historical baseline for N minutes).
- Add integration test that simulates migration on staging and measures batcher metrics before promotion.

Next actions / open items:
- [ ] Create a small hotfix PR to change migration default -> @Ravi to author (target: PR-hotfix-474).
- [ ] Add a gating check in CI to catch zero timeouts -> @Noah.
- [ ] Postmortem draft (start timeline + write-up) -> assignee: Maya (me).
- [ ] Expand observability: emit per-route batch_size.p50 in console dashboards -> eng-observability.

Notes / misc:
- KV cache investigation still worth finishing: check if namespace mapping changed during migration (some routes may have gotten new route IDs causing cache misses).
- Check customer-specific overrides that may have explicit zero set; ensure docs/SDK doesn't accidentally set 0 when client omits value.

Useful queries / instrumentation endpoints:
- /metrics -> batcher.batch_size.histogram, batcher.flush_interval.gauge, kvcache.hit_rate
- GET /debug/config/route/text-chat-v1 -> shows current runtime resolved settings
- logs: grep -R "flush_interval=0" /var/log/batcher*

Attachments / links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/472
- Jira: JIRA-INFR-893
- Console dashboard (canary): https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/batching-canary

If anyone picks this up: start by confirming the per-route timeout values in config store for the affected routes and temporarily set them to 50ms to observe recovery. If confirmed, block PR 472 migration and prepare hotfix.

-- Maya
